title: Machine-learning signatures of a high-risk lung pneumotype in critically ill patients
summary: Viral metagenomics and metatranscriptomics on 184 endotracheal aspirates from 94 intubated patients identified an unfavourable pneumotype, seen before hospital-acquired pneumonia, with virulent Streptococcus phages, temperate Klebsiella phages and increased Klebsiella pneumoniae activity. Machine-learning models defined two-viral-factor and four-bacterial-factor signatures predicting this pneumotype (AUC 0.8 and 0.7). In an independent cohort of 117 ICU patients (239 aspirates), the signatures were associated with mortality risk. Cohorts are small and observational, and machine learning is one of several analyses.
ai_technology: Machine-learning models defining viral and bacterial signatures that predict a high-risk pneumotype
organization: Lyon 1 Université; École Normale Supérieure de Lyon; Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

evidence.tested: Signature prediction of the pneumotype in 94 patients and replication of the mortality association in an independent cohort of 117 patients.
evidence.unknown: Causality and clinical utility; the machine-learning step is one analysis among several; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning models defined predictive microbial signatures.
